airport.name: Teniente General Gerardo Pérez Pinedo Airport

summary: Teniente General Gerardo Pérez Pinedo Airport (AYX) is a medium-sized regional airport serving Atalaya, a remote town in Peru's Ucayali region deep in the Amazon Basin. The facility provides a vital air link for the surrounding jungle communities, supporting both passenger travel and cargo operations to otherwise hard-to-reach areas. Its location along the Tambo and Urubamba rivers makes it an important gateway for travelers exploring the central Peruvian Amazon.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Teniente General Gerardo Pérez Pinedo Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by regional Peruvian carriers operating domestic flights, most commonly to and from Lima.

Q: How far is the airport from Atalaya's town center?
A: The airport is located just a short distance from Atalaya, typically reachable within a few minutes by road or river transport.

Q: Are there international flights from AYX?
A: No, the airport handles domestic flights only, with no scheduled international service.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a medium-sized regional airport, it offers basic passenger amenities including a small terminal building, but services are limited compared to larger Peruvian airports.
transport_tips: Taxis and mototaxis are typically available outside the terminal for the short transfer into Atalaya town. Many travelers continue onward by river boat, as Atalaya sits at the confluence of the Tambo and Urubamba rivers, so arranging combined land-and-river transport in advance is advisable. Roads in the region can be unpaved and weather-dependent, making flights the most reliable way to reach this remote area.
local_tip: If you're heading deeper into the Amazon after landing, coordinate your flight arrival with a pre-arranged river boat departure from Atalaya, since boats often follow their own schedules and don't wait for late flights.
